description: Variation of Condition Application under Section 73 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 to carry out development without compliance with Condition 1 (Approved Plans) of planning permission 20/02942/FUL (Part detailed/part outline planning permission for a mixed use development, incl demolition of existing buildings and erection of up to 2170 residential units (Use Class C3), 290sqm of flexible office floorspace (Use Class E),1395sqm of flexible retail/commercial floorspace (Use Class E/Sui Generis), 1250sqm community floorspace (Use Class F2), new publicly accessible open space and associated access, servicing, landscaping and works, incl stopping up of  all public highway incl Somerset Rd, Wimpole Close, Eureka Rd. St. Peters Rd, Burritt Rd, Stapleford Close, Willingham Way, Chesterton Terrace, Excelsior Close, Washington Rd, Somerset Rd and Franklin Close, various footpaths, parking courts and other areas of highway. Detailed permission for Phase 1 for erection of 452 residential units (Use Class C3), 1250sqm community floorspace (Use Class F2), 290sqm of flexible office floorspace (Use Class E), 395sqm of flexible retail/commercial floorspace (Use Class E/Sui Generis), new publicly accessible open space and associated access, servicing, parking, landscaping works incl tree removal, refuse/recycling and bicycle storage, energy centre and works. Outline permission for 1718 residential units (Use class C3), 1000sqm of flexible retail/commercial floorspace (Use Class E/Sui Generis) (with scale, layout, appearance, and landscaping reserved) is sought for the remainder of the development (parameter plans are included). Application accompanied by an Environmental Statement.) to amend parameter plans and design code.

decision_conditions: This development shall be begun within three years from the date of the original permission or within two years of the date of approval of the last of the Reserved Matters to be approved whichever is the later.Reason: To comply with Section 92 and Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990

This development shall be begun within three years from the date of the original permission or within two years of the date of approval of the last of the Reserved Matters to be approved whichever is the later.Reason: To comply with Section 92 and Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990

The approval of details of the following Reserved Matters shall be obtained from the local planning authority prior to commencement of that related phase or part thereof and the development shall be carried out only as approved: -- Appearance- Landscaping- Layout- ScaleReason: To comply with Section 92 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

No development authorised by any Reserved Matters approval shall be begun more than 12 years from the date of this permission or 2 years from the date of the final Reserved Matters approval, whichever is later, unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To comply with Section 92 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

The development shall be carried out within the scope tested in the scoped Environmental Impact Assessment, which was carried out for the approved drawings as listed under Condition 1 of this permission and incorporate the mitigation measures set out in the Environmental Statement dated November 2020 and Environmental Statement Addenda

The applications for the approval of Reserved Matters submitted under condition 4 shall be in accordance with the Design Guidelines, dated April 2021 or as the Design Guidelines as subsequently amended and agreed in writing by the local planning authority and in accordance with shall be in accordance with the Phasing, Demolition, Development Boundary Zones, and Scale set by the Parameter Plans.Each Application for reserved matters shall be accompanied by an updated Design and Access Statement including a section clearly highlighting any divergence from / interpretation of the Design Guidelines

The total gross external floorspace areas of the non-residential uses hereby approved shall be limited amaximum quantum of 2,935 sqm comprisingPhase 1 (Detailed)- 1,250sqm community floorspace (Use Class F2b)- 290 sqm of flexible office floorspace, (Use Class E(ci) E(cii) Ec(iii)- 395 sqm of flexible retail/commercial floorspace, (Use Class E(a) and E(b))Outline Phases- 1,000 sqm of flexible retail/commercial floorspace (Use Class E/Sui Generis)
KEPT INTENTIONALLY BLANK (No condition 9 on original permission)
KEPT INTENTIONALLY BLANK (No condition 10 on original permission)

Unless otherwise approved in writing by the local planning authority on an application pursuant to this condition no individual Class E(a) unit (as defined in the Use Class Order 1987 as amended) within the development shall exceed 300 sq.m, except the retail/commercial floorspace within Phase 1, unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority.

No Class E(a) unit (as defined in the Use Classes Order 1987 as amended) may be constructed subject to this planning permission nor shall be subsequently combined with an adjoining unit of the same use class, if the amalgamation would result in a combined unit that exceeds 300 sq m, unless otherwise agreed in writing with the local planning authority.

The non-residential uses hereby approved shall not include use in connection with the hiring, distribution of or trading in motor vehicles, or in connection with driving instruction, unless otherwise agreed in writing.

No development shall commence, other than demolition, within a Development Plot or Phase until a detailed surface water drainage scheme for that Development Plot or Phase, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority (with the exception of Blocks B, C and E that have been approved under applications 22/02616/CLC, 22/03284/CLC and 24/01387/CLC). The scheme shall subsequently be implemented in accordance with the approved details before the development is completed.

Development shall not commence, other than demolition, in any Development Plot or Phase (with the exception of Blocks B, C and E that have been approved under application 22/02616/CLC, 20/02942/FUL and 24/01387/CLC) until a related drainage strategy detailing any on and/or off-site drainage works for that Phase has been submitted and approved in accordance with the approved Drainage Strategy Report.

Development shall not commence, other than demolition, in any Development Plot or Phase until Impact Studies of the existing water supply infrastructure for that Development Plot or Phase have been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority (with the exception of Blocks B, C and E that have been approved under application 22/03327/CLC, 22/03327/CLC and 24/02419/CLC). The studies should determine the magnitude of any new additional capacity required in the system and a suitable connection point.
DELETED (as per 24/01715/NMA)

The development permitted by this planning permission shall be carried out in accordance with the Flood Risk Assessment (FRA) April 2021. The mitigation measures in the FRA shall be fully implemented prior to occupation of each Development Plot or Phase and subsequently in accordance with the timing / phasing arrangements embodied within the scheme, or within any other period as may subsequently be agreed, in writing, by the local planning authority.An updated FRA shall be submitted with each reserved matters application submitted in accordance with Condition 4, unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority. The mitigation measures in the FRA shall be fully implemented prior to occupation of each Development Plot or Phase and subsequently in accordance with the timing / phasing arrangements embodied within the scheme, or within any other period as may subsequently be agreed, in writing, by the local planning authority.

Prior to the occupation in each Development Plot or Phase (with the exception of Blocks B and E that have been approved under application 24/01533/CLC and 24/02126/CLC) , a Flood Management Plan/Emergency Response Plan shall be produced and submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval in writing in accordance with the Flood Risk Assessment April 2021 recommendations. This shall include identification and provision of safe route(s) or safe refuge areas within the buildings for occupants to use during times of flood. The plan shall be implemented as approved, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

Prior to the commencement of development in each Development Plot or Phase, a Construction Ecological Management Plan including that Development Plot or Phase shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority (with the exception of Blocks B, C and E that have been approved under application 22/02970/CLC, 23/03545/CLC and 22/03329/CLC). The Construction Ecological Management Plan shall include:1. Details of the appointment of an Ecological Clerk of Works (advisor level);2. Measures to address any invasive non-native species discovered on site;3. Works to limit/ prevent ingress to the buildings by birds seeking to nest;4. Restrictions and limitations on the timing of works with regard to bird nesting season;5. Detail of the method statement for the removal of any trees (potential roost features for bats);6. Detail of the method statement / toolbox talk for demolition teams outlining what to look for with regard to protected species (bats) and what mitigation measures will be put in place if they are found to be on site;7. Measures to prevent mammals getting trapped within the site (hedgehogs);8. Methods to retain and protect mature trees throughout development to retain linear foraging and commuting habitat features (bats); and9. Details of construction lighting and any necessary mitigation measures to prevent light spill affecting features of biodiversity value.

Prior to commencement of development in each Development Plot or Phase a Construction and Environmental Management Plan (CEMP) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority (with the exception of Blocks B, C and E that have been approved under application 22/02609/CLC, 24/00325/CLC and 22/03275/CLC). The CEMP shall then be reviewed and updated prior to commencement of development in each Phase and an updated version submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval prior to commencement of development in each Phase unless it is agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority that no amended version is warranted.The CEMP shall include specific details for:1. the control of construction noise and vibration during hours of noisy activities; an updated Construction Logistics Plan (CLP) to include - a construction waste and material management, transportation and disposal strategy; including construction delivery booking and construction vehicle holding arrangements; site access and car parking arrangements; construction phasing and agreed routes; timings; travel plan for staff/personnel involved in construction.1. Air quality measures for the control and monitoring of emissions (including from construction vehicles), dust, fine particles and odours; a Dust Management Plan (DMP). The DMP will need to detail the measures to reduce the impacts during the construction phase.2. Construction traffic routing through the area and the site and the development site, including details of signage and an enforcement system for breach of its provisions;3. A low emission strategy for construction traffic and machinery;4. Piling or other penetrative methods of foundation design in relation to risks to underlying groundwater;5. Measures to protect controlled waters from construction processes and contamination;6. Measures to minimise cross contamination on site;7. Measures to deal with unexpected contamination on site;8. Measures for the protection of invertebrate species and enhancements for them, including provisions for dealing with any species that are discovered during the works, and a programme of timing for the works;9. Details of security of the construction site in relation to the boundary of the development site;10. Details of coordination with sites abutting the application boundary;11. Hours of construction and details to minimise disturbance to residents;12. Access through the site during works and upon completion of works in relation to any phasing, including the connections with any completed phases, and connections to the surrounding area and its network of cycle paths, roads and footpaths; and13. Any temporary works, including any boundary treatment around later phases.14. Provisions for pedestrians shall be fully accessible to all including people with disabilities. 15. Details of cranes and other tall construction equipment (including the details of obstacle lighting) - Such schemes shall comply with Advice Note 4 'Cranes and Other Construction Issues' (available at www.aoa.org.uk/policy-campaigns/operations-safety).The development shall not be undertaken otherwise than in accordance with the CEMP approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority, unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority.

All Non Road Mobile Machinery (NRMM) of net power of 37kW and up to and including 560kW used during the course of the demolition, site preparation and construction phases of the development shall comply with the emission standards set out in chapter 7 of the GLA's supplementary planning guidance 'Control of Dust and Emissions During Construction and Demolition' dated July 2014 (SPG) or any subsequent guidance. All major development sites in Greater London shall keep an inventory on site and on the online register at: https://nrmm.london/ of all NRMM between 37kW and 560kW. All NRMM shall meet Stage IIIA of EU Directive 97/68/EC (as amended) as a minimum within Greater London (Stage IIIB from 1st September 2020) and Stage IIIB of EU Directive 97/68/EC as a minimum within the Central Activity Zone (Stage IV from 1st September 2020).

No retained tree shall be cut down, uprooted or destroyed, nor shall any retained tree be pruned other than in accordance with the approved drawings and specifications, without the written approval of the Local Planning Authority (with the exception of Blocks B, C and E that have been approved under application 22/02610/CLC, 24/00370/CLC and 22/03276/CLC). Any pruning shall be carried out in accordance with British Standard 3998:2010 Tree work and in accordance with any supplied Arboricultural Development Statement. If any retained tree is removed, uprooted or destroyed or dies, another tree shall be planted at the same place and that tree shall be of such size and species, and shall be planted at such time, as may be specified in writing by the Local Planning Authority Tree protection shall be maintained in-situ and not moved or removed until all construction has finished, and equipment, materials, or machinery are removed from the relevant Development Plot or Phase.All arboricultural protection information and plans submitted as part of the application, and listed in the approved drawings condition, shall be implemented and adhered to at all times during the construction process unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority. This shall include a timetable of arboricultural site supervision.(a) Details of the means of protecting the trees (in line BS5837:2012) within each Development Plot or Phase which are to be retained from damage during building works shall be submitted to and approved by the local planning authority before the start of any demolition, building or other works. Such protection shall be installed and retained as approved throughout the period of works.(b) No development shall take place until tree protection measures are installed and any further information is provided in accordance with the submitted arboricultural information. The applicant shall arrange a pre commencement meeting with the Local Planning Authority and the applicant's project arboriculturalist to allow inspection of the protection measures once in situ. In this condition 'retained tree' means an existing tree or hedge, which is to be retained in accordance with the approved drawings and specifications. Paragraphs (a) and (b) below shall have effect until the expiration of 5 years fromthe first occupation of the developm, unless the retained tree forms part of the approved wind mitigation strategy, if so, Paragraphs (a) and (b) shall have effect in perpetuity.

No impact piling shall take place within any Development Plot or Phase until a piling method statement (detailing the depth and type of piling to be undertaken and the methodology by which such piling will be carried out, including measures to prevent and minimise the potential for damage to subsurface sewerage infrastructure, and the programme for the works) has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority (with the exception of Blocks B, C and E that have been approved under application 22/02731/CLC and 20/01559/CLC). Any piling must be undertaken in accordance with the terms of the approved piling method statement.

A) No development (other than demolition to existing ground level) (with the exception of Blocks B, C and E that have been approved under application 22/021617/CLC) shall take place until the applicant (or their heirs and successors in title) has secured the implementation of a programme of archaeological evaluation in accordance with a written scheme which has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority and a report on that evaluation has been submitted to the local planning authority.B) If heritage assets of archaeological interest are identified by the evaluation under Part A, then before the commencement of development (other than demolition to existing ground level) the applicant (or their heirs and successors in title) shall secure the implementation of a programme of archaeological investigation in accordance with a Written Scheme of Investigation which has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authorityC) No development (other than demolition to existing ground level) shall take place other than in accordance with the Written Scheme of Investigation approved under Part (B)D) The development shall not be occupied until the site investigation and post investigation assessment has been completed in accordance with the programme set out in the Written Scheme of Investigation approved under Part (B), and the provision for analysis, publication and dissemination of the results and archive deposition has been secured

If, during development within any Development Plot or Phase, contamination not previously identified is found to be present at the site then no further development (unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority) shall be carried out within that Phase until the developer has submitted, and obtained written approval from the Local Planning Authority(with the exception of Block B that has been approved under application 20/01559/CLC), for a remediation strategy detailing how this unsuspected contamination shall be dealt with. The remediation strategy shall be implemented as approved, verified and reported to the satisfaction of the Local Planning Authority.Prior to occupation of development within a Development Plot or Core, a verification report demonstrating the completion of works set out in the approved remediation strategy and the effectiveness of the remediation shall be submitted to, and approved in writing, by the local planning authority. The submission shall include a phasing plan for the relevant phase, that clearly shows the part of the Site that the verification report relates to and the proposed sequence for completion of the remaining verification reports for the relevant phase.The report shall include results of sampling and monitoring carried out in accordance with the approved verification plan to demonstrate that the site remediation criteria have been met. To ensure that the site does not pose any further risk to human health or the water environment by demonstrating that the requirements of the approved verification plan have been met and that remediation of the site is complete.

Where appropriate, prior to the installation of external ventilation equipment, including ducting, details shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval, in association with those reserved matters submitted pursuant to Condition 4, where appropriate, and shall be installed in accordance with those details approved by the Local Planning Authority

Prior to the construction of fire hydrants (other than for demolition and site Enabling Works) in any Development Plot or Phase, details for the provision of fire hydrants within that Development Plot or Phase shall be submitted and approved in writing by the local planning authority (with the exception of Block B, C and E that have been approved under application 22/02733/CLC, 22/03330/CLC and 24/01388/CLC). The fire hydrants should be sited within the footpath, one metre clear of obstructions, with the outlets no more than 300mm below ground level. The hydrants should conform to BS:750 andbe indicated with a hydrant indicator plate conforming to BS:3251.

Prior to the commencement of development (other than demolition, site enabling works) in any Phase or Development Plot, details of the number, layout, location and access to residential car parking spaces to be provided for that phase shall be submitted to the local planning authority (with the exception of Block B, C and E that have been approved under application 22/02618/CLC, 22/03288/CLC, 25/01053/CLC) for approval and then provided and maintained in accordance with the approved details.

A Parking Management Strategy and Car Park Management Plan for each relevant Phase or Development Plot shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority (with the exception of Block B and E that have been approved under application 25/00477/CLC) for approval in writing prior to commencement of use of any car parking in that Phase. This shall provide a strategy for car park management including:1. means of separating any operational and residential parking and enforcing that separation;2. allocation of residential spaces between market and affordable units,3. service charges;4. allocation of parking for people with disabilities;5. car club allocation;6. charging points for electric vehicles;7. cycle parking/storage differentiated by residential and other users;8. access controls to the underground parking and emergency vehicle route; handling the relationship between private and service vehicles; and9. Provision of parking for (not operating) trades vehicles i.e large vans

Details of the number, layout, design, location and access to cycle parking spaces for each of the uses within an identified Phase or Development Plot, including, design, position, size, and method of implementation, shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval in writing inassociation with details submitted pursuant to Condition 4. The cycle parking provided shall be as approved by the local planning authority and shall be retained for use of residents, visitors, and workers of the development.

Residential and commercial travel plans shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval in writing prior to the occupation of each Phase of development or Development Plot (with the exception of Block B and E that have been approved under application 24/01489/CLC and 24/02115/CLC). The Travel Plans shall be provided to residents and implemented in accordance with the approved documents.

90% of the dwellings shall comply with Building Regulations Requirement Approved Document M4(2) Category 2: Accessible and adaptable dwellings and 10% of the residential units provided shall be capable of easy adaptation to Building Regulations Approved Document M4(3) Category 3: (Wheelchair user dwellings).Prior to the occupation of development within a Phase or Development Plot involving residential dwellings, an Accessible Homes Strategy shall have been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority (with the exception of Block B and E that have been approved under application 24/01400/CLC and 24/02317/CLC ). The Accessible Homes Strategy shall ensure that the M4(3) units are delivered in homes of varying typologies, tenures and locations. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved strategy.

Prior to the commencement of development (other than demolition and site enabling works) in any Phase or Development Plot (Other than Phase 1), details of mitigation for wind, including roof top enclosures, to be submitted for approval in writing by the Local Planning Authority for that phase (with the exception of Blocks B, C and E that have been approved under application 22/02619/CLC, 22/03289/CLC and 23/03525/CLC). The scheme approved by the Local Planning Authority shall be fully implemented and maintained.

Prior to the occupation of development within a Phase or Development Plot involving residential dwellings, details of the noise measures for that Phase (the Noise Assessment) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority (with the exception of Blocks B and E that have been approved under application 24/02261/CLC and 25/02337/CLC). The Noise Assessment shall provide details of the necessary mitigation works for that phase of development to protect the residential accommodation hereby approved from external noise sources, in order to meet the appropriate internal noise levels, set out in BS8233. This may include details of fenestration, and balustrade and screen design to balconies, including fixing windows or other demonstrable mitigation, and details of ventilation.That Phase of development shall be designed in accordance with the mitigation measures in the report, and the mitigation measures shall be fully implemented prior to first occupation of the residential accommodation to which it relates.

Prior to the occupation of non-residential / commercial development in any Development Plot or Phase, details of noise insulation measures of the non- residential / commercial uses to provide effective resistance to the transmission of airborne sound (including amplified music) and impact sound horizontally and/or vertically between those units in that Phase and any residential unit (C3) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The internal noise levels will be designed to meet the appropriate levels set out in BS 8233. The approved measures shall be implemented prior to the commencement of the non-residential uses.

Prior to the commencement of development (other than demolition and site enabling works) in each Development Plot or Phase, details of a Sustainable Waste Strategy, including details of the storage and segregation of waste for that phase, shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval in writing in association with the details required under Condition 4. Each Development Plot or Phase shall be implemented and maintained in accordance with the Sustainable Waste Strategy approved by the Local Planning Authority (with the exception of Blocks B, C and E that have been approved under application 22/02620/CLC, 22/03290/CLC and 24/01205/CLC).

Prior to the occupation of the non-residential units, details of any outside forecourt/outdoor space for those units associated with any of the non- residential uses hereby approved are to be submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval in writing, including details of location, hours of use and any boundary treatment and furniture (temporary or permanent) prior to any use of such areas. The forecourt/outdoor spaces shall not be implemented other than in line with those details approved by the Local Planning Authority in writing, and in accordance with the with the approved Park Management Plan, where appropriate.

Prior to the first occupation of development in any Phase or Development Plot, a Play Equipment and Surfaces Maintenance and Management Plan shall be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority (with the exception of Blocks B and E that have been approved under application 24/01385/CLC and 24/02128/CLC). detailing levels of inspection (visual, operation and annual) and anticipated maintenance costs (including safety surfacing, water treatment) per year, at 3, 5, and 7 years after installation together with the anticipated life-span before replacement, and the Phase or Development Plot shall be implemented and maintained in accordance with the approved Play Equipment and Surfaces Maintenance and Management Plan.

Prior to the first occupation of development in any Phase or Development Plot, a biodiversity method statement for the provision of the Biodiversity Net Gain delivered through habitat creation and / or enhancement within that phase or development plot indicating the:a) appointment of an Ecological Clerk of Works (advisor level);b) detailed design of the (re)creation of biodiversity habitats and features within the open space;c) details of Biodiversity Net Gain calculation using the biodiversity metric 3 calculation toold) type and source of plants to be used for biodiversity habitats (locally native species of local provenance unless otherwise agreed in writing); ande) initial aftercare and maintenance to ensure habitat establishment shall be submitted for approval by the Local Planning Authority (with the exception of Block B that has been approved under application 24/01892/CLC) and the Phase or Development Plot shall be implemented and maintained in accordance with the approved Biodiversity Method Statement

Prior to the first occupation of the development an Open Space Management Plan for the relevant phase will be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The management of the new Park, as part of the wider public realm provision, will be carried out in accordance with the approved Open Space and Park Management Plan, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

Notwithstanding any materials specified in the application, details and samples of materials proposed to be used on all external surfaces of the development in a Development Plot or Phase shall be submitted to and approved by the local planning authority (with the exception of Blocks B and E that have been approved under application 23/01236/CLC, 24/02220/CLC, 24/01153/CLC and 24/00849/CLC). before any installation of such materials in that Detailed or Outline Phase.In addition the developer shall display the sample materials on a 'mock-up' of each phase, the details of the mock-up to be agreed with the local planning authority. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details.

Prior to its installation details of any external lighting associated with the development including levels of illumination, position, design, structure, direction of illumination, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority (with the exception of Blocks B, C and E that have been approved under application 24/00911/CLC, 25/00167/CLC and 25/02622/CLC). The development shall be implemented and maintained in accordance with those details as may be approved.

Prior to the first occupation of development in any Phase or Development Plot, a Biodiversity Lighting Strategy shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority (with the exception of Blocks B and E that have been approved under application 25/00168/CLC and 25/00168/CLC) to Include:- identification of those areas/features that are particularly designed to retain ecological functionality and/or enhance biodiversity across the whole site (both built environment and landscaping);- show how and where external lighting will be installed in accordance with "Guidance note 08/18 Bats and Artificial Lighting in the UK" produced by the Institute of Lighting Professionals.All external lighting shall be installed and maintained in accordance with the specifications and locations set out in the approved strategy, and these shall be maintained thereafter in accordance with the approved strategy.

Prior to the commencement of development of the Blocks containing the Energy Centres, details of the Energy Centres, including plans and sections, showing the position (both horizontally and vertically) and physical form of the energy centre shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority (with the exception of Blocks E that has been approved under application 22/03277/CLC) for approval together with details of the proposed plant in connection with the details approved within the Energy Strategy (or as subsequently updated). This should include details of how the Energy Centres shall have capacity toserve the energy needs of the site and connect to the District Heating Network taking account of the District Heating Network Statement required to be submitted to the Local Planning Authority and the results of the Energy Master Plan study for the area. Details shall be included on the phased introduction of capacity to supply and achieve energy efficiencies and contributions to the CO2 emission reductions to be achieved for each Development Plot or Phase including information on the proposed distribution network and its linkage to the buildings and District Heating Network, unless otherwise demonstrated to be unfeasible. The energy centre shall have a size as is demonstrated to the Local Planning Authority's satisfaction would meet the capacity requirements of the development.The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details.

No later than 6 months after occupation of use of each of the non-residential uses a Post Construction Certificate verifying that at least 'Very Good' BREEAM level has been achieved unless otherwise agreed in writing beforehand, shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority. Reason: To ensure the implementation of sustainable design, low carbon development and renewable energy

Details of the location, layout and specification of any Photovoltaic Panels to be installed on the roof of the buildings as subsequently detailed within the Reserved Matters applications, shall be submitted for approval by the Local Planning Authority and shall be installed prior to occupation and maintained in accordance with the approved details.

For each Development Plot or Phase, a detailed accessibility statement and management plan (including a programme for implementation) shall be submitted outlining those measures proposed to ensure an accessible and inclusive environment, both internally and externally, including but not limited to, pedestrian routes, lift specifications, accessible toilet provision, access points along with blue badge spaces. Such a statement is to be approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority (with the exception of Blocks B, C and E that have been approved under application 22/03659/CLC, 23/01295/CLC and 24/01238/CLC). The development shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with the approved details.

There shall be no occupation of any commercial or residential unit within a plot or phase until provision is made for the storage of refuse/ recycling awaiting collection to serve that plot (including a strategy to deal with bulky waste) according to details which shall previously have been agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority (with the exception of Blocks B and E that have been approved under application 24/01491/CLC and 24/02117/CLC). Unless otherwise agreed in writing these details shall include provision for suitable containment and segregation of recyclable waste. The measures shall be fully implemented and maintained in accordance with the agreed details for the development or the relevant phases thereof as the case may be.

The residential component of the development hereby permitted shall achieve as a minimum 63% reduction in carbon dioxide emissions over Part L of the Building Regulations (2013) secured on site as declared in the submitted Energy Statement November 2020.An updated Energy Strategy shall be submitted for approval by the local planning authority with all the reserved matters applications submitted in accordance with Condition 4.The development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved updated Strategy and thereafter maintained.

The non-residential component of the development hereby permitted shall achieve as a minimum 45% reduction in carbon dioxide emissions over Part L of the Building Regulations (2013) secured on site as declared in the submitted Energy Statement November 2020.An updated Energy Strategy shall be submitted for approval by the local planning authority with all the reserved matters applications submitted in accordance with Condition 4.The development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved updated Strategy and thereafter maintained.

Unless specified on the approved drawings, no lights (excluding aviation lights), meter boxes, flues, vents or pipes, and no telecommunications equipment masts or equipment or associated structures, alarm boxes, television aerials or satellite dishes shall be fixed or installed on the external face or roofs of the buildings, without the prior approval in writing of the local planning authority

Prior to first occupation of each phase or plot of development hereby approved, details of all proposed walls, fences and boundary treatments shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority (with the exception of Block B that has been approved under application 24/01643/CLC). The boundary treatment(s) shall then be carried out in accordance with the approved details and retained permanently thereafter to the satisfaction of the Local Planning Authority.

A. Prior to the commencement of the relevant phase or plot (other than demolition, site clearance and ground works), a Fire Statement for the relevant phase or plot, in the form of an independent fire strategy produced by a third party suitably qualified assessor shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority (with the exception of Blocks B, C and E that have been approved under application 22/02808/CLC, 22/03330/CLC and 24/01023/CLC). The statement should detail how the development proposal will function in terms of:The building's construction: methods, products and materials used, including manufacturer's details;The means of escape for all building users: stair cores, escape for building users who are disabled or require level access, and the associated evacuation strategy approach;Features which reduce the risk to life: fire alarm systems, passive and active fire safety measures and associated management and maintenance plans;Access for fire service personnel and equipment: how this will be achieved in an evacuation situation, water supplies, provision and positioning of equipment, firefighting lifts, stairs and lobbies, any fire suppression and smoke ventilation systems proposed, and the ongoing maintenance and monitoring of these;How provision will be made within the site to enable fire appliances to gain access to buildings; andEnsuring that any potential future modifications to the building will take into account and not compromise the base build fire safety/ protection measures.The development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved Fire Statement and retained as such for the lifetime of the development.B. Prior to commencement for each building details shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority demonstrating that a minimum of at least one lift per core (or more subject to capacity assessments) will be a suitably sized fire evacuation lift suitable to be used to evacuate people who require level access from the building (with the exception of Blocks B, C and E that have been approved under application 22/02808/CLC, 22/03330/CLC and 24/01023/CLC). The development shall be carried out in accordance with these details and maintained as such in perpetuity.

Prior to the commencement of each Phase of the Development, if more than 30 months elapse between the date of the approved Ecological Surveys and commencement of development, updated preliminary ecological assessments shall be undertaken for the relevant phase and submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority (with the exception of Blocks B and C that has been approved under application 22/02621/CLC and 23/03526/CLC).Such surveys are to be carried out by a suitably qualified ecologist and accompanied by a report confirming the results and implications of the assessment, including any revised mitigation measures.All approved mitigation measures as approved shall be implemented and maintained in full in accordance with the agreed time scales.

No use within a Development Plot or Phase of the development hereby permitted shall be occupied until a Servicing and Delivery Management Plan (SDMP) for that use has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority (with the exception of Blocks B and E that has been approved under application 24/01490/CLC and 24/02124/CLC). The uses hereby permitted shall thereafter be operated in accordance with the approved details.The submitted details must include (but not be limited to) the following):(a) frequency of deliveries to the site;(b) frequency of other servicing vehicles such as refuse collections;(c) dimensions of delivery and servicing vehicles;(d) proposed loading and delivery locations;(e) a strategy to manage vehicles servicing the site;(f) The hours/days of deliveries for vehicles and the precautions and measure to be taken to mitigate noise impacts;

Prior to the first use/occupation of the development within any phase, a detailed Signage and Wayfinding Strategy for that Phase shall be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority.The development shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with the details and drawings thus approved.Prior to the substantial completion of the development within any phase, a detailed Signage and Wayfinding Strategy for that Phase shall be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with the details and drawings thus approved.

No development within a Development Plot or Phase, shall commence until a scheme for temporary fencing and/or enclosure of the site (a Hoarding Strategy) has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority (with the exception of Blocks B, C and E that have been approved under application 22/02624/CLC, 22/03279/CLC and 24/00326/CLC), and the temporary fencing and/or enclosure has been erected in accordance with the approved details. The temporary fencing and/or enclosure shall thereafter be retained for the duration of the demolition and building works in accordance with the approved details. No part of the temporary fencing and/or enclosure shall be used for the display of advertisement hoardings, unless consent is sought for the Local Planning Authority.The Developer shall explore options for a living wall hoarding.

Prior to implementing any works for any temporary uses or structures including sales/marketing suites within the site, save for any buildings or temporary structures necessary for the works of demolition or construction hereby approved, details shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority (with the exception of Blocks B, C and E that have been approved under application 23/02518/CLC, 24/00907/CLC and 25/01746/CLC). Any (interim/semipermanent) structures, uses and buildings shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details, for a specified time period setout in the details and shall be discontinued/removed once the temporary period has been expired.

Prior to commencement of demolition works in each Development Plot or Phase a Demolition Method Statement shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority (with the exception of Blocks B, C and E that have been approved under application 22/02611/CLC, 23/01203/CLC and 24/00327/CLC). Details shall include control measures for dust, noise, vibration (piling), lighting, delivery locations, restriction of hours of work and all associated activities audiblebeyond the site boundary, advance notification to neighbours and other interested parties of proposed works and public display of contact details including accessible phone contact to persons responsible for the site works for the duration of the works for that Development Plot or Phase.No demolition shall commence until a risk assessment based on the Mayor's Best Practice Guidance (The control of dust and emissions from construction and demolition) has been undertaken and a method statement for emissions control (including an inventory and timetable of dust generating activities, emission control methods and where appropriate air quality monitoring) has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The appropriate mitigation measures to minimise dust and emissions must be incorporated into the site specific Demolition Method Statement and Construction Management Plan. Developers must ensure that on-site contractors follow best practicable means to minimise dust and emissions at all times.Demolition works shall be undertaken in accordance with the approved Demolition Method Statement.

No plant, water tanks, water tank enclosures or other structures, that are not shown on the approved plans for the detailed phase and any subsequent plans approved under Reserved Matters Applications, shall be erected upon the roofs of the buildings hereby permitted unless approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

Prior to the occupation of each Development Plot, or phase a scheme showing full details of the following for that phase shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority (with the exception of Blocks B and E that have been approved under application 24/02154/CLC and 24/02155/CLC).(a) CCTV;(b) Security lightingand the development shall be implemented (and maintained) in accordance with the approved details

Prior to the occupation of each Development Plot an Estate Management and Maintenance Plan for that Phase in which development would be located, setting out maintenance and management responsibilities for all communal play spaces, public realm, communal amenity spaces and all publicly accessible open spaces, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority (with the exception of Blocks B and E that have been approved under application 24/01463/CLC and 24/02125/CLC). and the open spaces shall thereafter be maintained and managed in accordance with the approved details.

The non-residential floorspace hereby approved plan shall be used only for purposes within Class E and F2 (excluding in connection with the hiring, distribution of or trading in motor vehicles, or in connection with driving instruction), unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority.

Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (or any Order revoking and/or re-enacting that Order) and Section 55 of the Town and Country Planning Act (As Amended) the premises shall only be used for the purposes listed in Condition 8 and for no other purpose (including any other purpose in Class E or F of Town and Country Planning (Use Classes) Order 1987 or any provision equivalent to that Class in any Statutory Instrument revoking and/or re- enacting that Order.

Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) Order 2015, or any future enactment of that Order, no windows, doors or glazed areas (other than such as may be shown on the approved plans) shall be formed in any wall of the buildings without the prior written consent of the local planning authority.

Details of hard and soft landscaping, habitat features for protected species and treatment of parts of the site not covered by buildings, to include species of new planting and any existing plants/trees to be retained for each Development Plot or Phase, shall be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority (with the exception of Blocks B, C and E that have been approved under application 24/00912/CLC, 24/02127/CLC and 25/01745/CLC) before the relevant works are commenced. Details are to include tree planting pit cross-sections with full details of soil volume provision (quantities andlocations for each species) of trees planted in hard landscaping. All planting, seeding or turfing included in the approved details shall be carried out prior to the occupation of any part of the development, or in accordance with a programme agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority. Any trees or plants planted as part of the approved landscape scheme for each Phase or Development Plot or Phase, which within a period of five years from when the trees or plants are planted are found to be dead, removed, or becomes seriously damaged or diseased, shall be replaced in the next planting seasonwith others of similar size and species, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the local planning authority.

Detailed plans of biodiversity provision, including a programme of works, shall be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority (with the exception of Block B that has been approved under application 24/01426/CLC) before the relevant works are commenced. This shall include the types and location of boxes for bats and birds (black redstart and house sparrow) integrated into the built fabric; locations shown on appropriately scaled maps and plans; timetable for implementation, demonstrating that works are aligned with the proposed phasing of construction.The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved materials and maintained thereafter.

Details of the amount and spatial distribution of non-residential uses within the subsequent outline blocks/plots, including details of the size, façade treatment, opening times, disabled access and toilets for each unit shall be submitted to and in approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to occupation of each unit. The uses shall only be operated in accordance with the details approved by the local planning authority.

A scheme detailing the provision and maintenance of green roofs for each Development Plot shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority prior to the occupation of the Development Plot (with the exception of Block B that has been approved under application 24/01640/CLC). This shall include details of how these roofs will provide habitats and features for biodiversity (in accordance with definition of an extensive biodiverse roof and advice provided in The GRO Green Roof Code 2014). The agreed scheme shall be implemented as approved prior to first occupation of the development and thereafter maintained in accordance with the approved scheme.

Details of an internal road management plan for the highway layout as indicated on the approved detailed phase and any subsequent plans approved under Reserved Matters Applications shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval prior to the first occupation (with the exception of Blocks B and E that has been approved under application 25/00477/CLC and 25/00477/CLC). The management plan should include the following details:(i) details of how the internal roads would link to and adjacent sites;(ii) how vehicular traffic would be managed along the identified routes; and(iii) design details of the internal roads, footpaths and cycleways (including design, materials, dimensions, alignment, maintenance, accessibility).The management plan shall be implemented in accordance with such details as may be approved and retained thereafter.

Prior to the commencement of development in any Phase or Development Plot other than Phase 1 the following information should be submitted An updated Supplementary Transport Assessment (STA) with updated trip generation, distribution and mode share forecasts, and any mitigation measures required shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.The STAs should include additional traffic surveys and junction modelling (individually and/or linked) agreed by RBK Highways prior to submission Any mitigation measures proposed should be supported by a Road Safety Audit.The approved measures shall be implemented / delivered in accordance with a timeframe to be agreed as part of the STA submission.

Prior to the commencement of development in any Phase or Development Plot (other than Phase 1) the following information should be submitted:- Wind / Microclimate assessment to be submitted with each phase- Secure by Design assessment- Daylight / Sunlight assessment

Details of the number, layout, design, location, charging provision, and access to mobility scooter spaces for each of the uses within an identified Phase or Development Plot, including, design, position, size, and method of implementation, shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval in writing in association with details submitted pursuant to Condition 4.The approved mobility scooter parking provision for each phase or plot shall be made available prior to the first occupation of the phase / plot and shall thereafter be retained for use of residents and visitors to the development.

Prior to the occupation of any unit in each Development Plot or Phase a scheme for protecting dwellings from noise, including glazing specification, shall have been submitted to, and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority (with the exception of Blocks B and E that has been approved under application 24/02261/CLC and 25/02337/CLC). The scheme shall achieve the following noise levels:- Internal day time (0700 - 2300) noise levels shall not exceed 35dB LAeq, 16hrfor habitable rooms (bedrooms and living rooms)- Internal night time (2300 - 0700) noise levels shall not exceed 30dB, 8hr LAeq with individual noise events not exceeding 45dB LAmax on more than 15 occasions during the night time (2300 - 0700) in accordance with Council guidelines.The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details and thereafter maintained.

Prior to the commencement of any phase or development plot above ground level, detailed drawings at a scale of 1:5 of the following features shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority (with the exception of Block B that has been approved under application 23/01612/CLC):- Windows, including any aprons, sills, mouldings, heads, jambs, transoms, mullions, lintels or reveals- Entrance details, canopy / overhang details Gates, fencing, glazing systems- Balconies / terraces (including privacy screens) Railings, parapets / datums- Facade recesses, projections, spandrels and shadow gaps Brick coursing details- Publicly visible rainwater goods- Vents (intake and exhaust), grilles and any other public visible ventilation openings- Green, biodiverse roofs Roof plant enclosure- Tree pits, planters and greening Surfacing and SUDs- Street furniture and play equipment Boundary treatment details- Front garden landscaping details Communal amenity landscaping details- Cycle parking details External- Bin store detailsThe developer shall submit a site plan / elevation and key plans / elevations where applicable associated with each detail identifying the location of each typical detail. The development shall then be carried out in accordance with the approved drawings.

Prior to the commencement of any phase or development plot, plans shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority (with the exception of Blocks B, C and E that have been approved under application 22/02612/CLC, 22/03280/CLC and 23/03527/CLC), demonstrating the provision of sufficient ducting space for full fibre connectivity infrastructure within the development. The development shall be carried out in accordance with these plans and maintained as such in perpetuity.

Each application for reserved matters submitted in accordance with Condition 4 shall be accompanied by a detailed Circular Economy Statement and Operational Waste Management Strategy in line with the GLA's Circular Economy Statement Guidance, which shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The statement shall adhere to the principles set out in the draft Circular Economy Statement.The development shall be carried out in accordance with the details so approved.

Prior to the occupation of any phase / development plot, a Post Completion Report setting out the predicted and actual performance against all numerical targets in the relevant Circular Economy Statement shall be submitted to the GLA at: CircularEconomyLPG@london.gov.uk, along with any supporting evidence as per the GLA's Circular Economy Statement Guidance. The Post Completion Report shall provide updated versions of Tables 1 and 2 of the Circular Economy Statement, the Recycling and Waste Reporting form and Bill of Materials. Confirmation of submission to the GLA shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the local planning authority, prior to occupation (with the exception of Blocks B and E that have been approved under application 24/02796/CLC and 24/02796/CLC).

Prior to the occupation of each building the post-construction tab of the GLA's whole life carbon assessment template should be completed accurately and in its entirety in line with the GLA's Whole Life Carbon Assessment Guidance. The post-construction assessment should provide an update of the information submitted at the planning submission stage, including the whole life carbon emission figures for all life-cycle modules based on the actual materials, products and systems used. This should be submitted to the GLA at: ZeroCarbonPlanning@london.gov.uk, along with any supporting evidence as per the guidance. Confirmation of submission to the GLA shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by the local planning authority, prior to occupation of the relevant building (with the exception of Blocks B and E that have been approved under application 24/02795/CLC).

Each application for reserved matters submitted in accordance with Condition 4 shall be accompanied by a revised Air Quality Neutral Assessment (AQNA). The AQNA shall demonstrate that each phase/plot remains within the air quality neutral benchmarks. The mitigation measures in the AQNA shall be fully implemented prior to occupation of each Development Plot or Phase and subsequently in accordance with the timing / phasing arrangements embodied within the scheme, or within any other period as may subsequently be agreed, in writing, by the local planning authority.

Each application for reserved matters submitted in accordance with Condition 4 shall be accompanied by an Air Quality Assessment. The Air Quality Assessment shall demonstrate that future occupants are not exposed to poor air quality arising from emissions from the site-wide heat network. The mitigation measures in the AQA shall be fully implemented prior to occupation of each Development Plot or Phase and subsequently in accordance with the timing / phasing arrangements embodied within the scheme, or within any other period as may subsequently be agreed, in writing, by the local planning authority.
DELETED (as per 26/01704/NMA)

Prior to the commencement of above ground works of each phase or development plot an updated Urban Greening Factor Assessment (UGF) shall have been submitted to the local planning authority and approved in writing (with the exception of Blocks B and E that have been approved under application 23/00895/CLC and 23/00895/CLC).The updated UGF shall use the Greater London Authority Urban Greening Factor calculator available at the time of the submission.The updated UGF shall demonstrate all efforts to exceed a score of 0.4. UGF.

An Affordable Housing strategy including the tenure distribution plan shall be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority (with the exception of Blocks B, C and E which has been approved under application 22/02613/CLC, 22/03281/CLC and 24/01182/CLC) prior to the commencement of any phase or any development within a Plot.

The development hereby permitted shall incorporate security measures to minimise the risk of crime and to meet the specific security needs of the development in accordance with the principles and objectives of Secured by Design. Details of these measures for each phase or plot shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to commencement of the development (excluding demolition) (with the exception of Blocks B, C and E that have been approved under application 22/02730/CLC, 22/03675/CLC and 24/01024/CLC), and shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details prior to occupation.

Prior to occupation of development within a Development Plot or Core, a Secured By Design final certificate shall be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority (with the exception of Blocks B that has been approved under application 25/01507/CLC). The submission shall include a phasing plan for the relevant phase, that clearly shows the part of the Site that the Secured By Design final certificate relates to and the proposed sequence for completion of the remaining Secured By Design final certificates for the relevant phase.

No development of a plot or phase shall commence until a site investigation scheme based on the desk study together with assessment of risks posed by any contamination is carried out in accordance with British Standard BS10175: Investigation of Potentially Contaminated Sites - Code of Practice and the Environment Agency's Model Procedures for the Management of Land Contamination (CLR 11) (or equivalent British Standard and Model Procedures if replaced), has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority (with the exception of Blocks B and C that has been approved under application 22/02614/CLC and 23/03528/CLC). Should remediation be required, no development shall commence until a report specifying the measures to be taken, including the timescale, to remediate the site to render it suitable for use shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority

Details shall be submitted to the local planning authority of the ground level of each phase across each phase prior to the commencement of each phase (with the exception of Blocks B and C that have been approved under application 22/02615/CLC and 24/01239/CLC). The development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details.Prior to any above ground works (excluding demolition) details shall be submitted to and approved by the local planning authority of the ground level of each plot to demonstrate adequate access for all users. The development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details.

The site and building works required to implement the development shall be only carried out between the hours of 08.00 and 18.00 Mondays to Fridays and between 08.00 and 13.00 on Saturdays and not at all on Bank Holidays and Sundays.

Prior to above ground works, details of the boilers hereby approved shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority (with the exception of Block B that has been approved under application 23/01570/CLC). The boilers shall have dry Nox emissions not exceeding 40 mg/kWh. The boilers shall be installed and retained for the lifetime of the development in accordance with the approved details unless the prior written approval of the authority is given.

No development in any Phase or Development Plot shall be occupied until confirmation has been provided that either:- all water network upgrades required to accommodate the additional flows to serve the development in any Phase or Development Plot have been completed; or- a development and infrastructure phasing plan has been agreed with Thames Water to allow the development in any Phase or Development Plot to be occupied.Where a development and infrastructure phasing plan is agreed no occupation shall take place other than in accordance with the agreed housing and infrastructure phasing plan.

The details for the provision of the community centre and any associated indoor sports facilities shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority after consultation with Sport England and prior to laying of the damp proof course in the external brickwork for Block C, Phase 1. The development hereby permitted shall not be carried out other than in accordance with the approved details.

The details for the provision of the rifle club shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority after consultation with Sport England prior to commencement of Phase 3. Phase 3 Shall not commence until the details have been approved in writing.

No Development shall commence, other than demolition, within any Development Plot or Phase unless and until all interests in such Development Plot or Phase that need to be bound to ensure satisfactory enforcement of the obligations contained in the Section 111/Section 106 Agreement between The Mayor and Burgesses of The Royal Borough of Kingston Upon Thames and Cambridge Road (RBK) LLLP dated 29 July 2022 are bound to the reasonable satisfaction (as confirmed in writing) of the Local Planning Authority.
